tagline: Website builder with templates, AI tools, e-commerce, bookings, and apps.
verdictSummary: The one specific business website you need — a static site with clean copy, a working contact form, solid SEO basics baked in at build time — is a real weekend build. What doesn't come with it is Wix as a platform: a visual drag-and-drop editor, an app marketplace, and built-in e-commerce and booking tools.
coreLoopDIY: A static site with copy in plain content files, a working contact form, and SEO fundamentals — a sitemap, meta tags, structured data — generated automatically at build time.
whyPeopleStillPay: One website project tends to turn into ten ongoing maintenance requests — people pay so those keep being handled without hiring anyone.
notes: Worth comparing against the Webflow and Framer entries in this catalogue — the DIY-site-versus-site-builder distinction is the same story each time.
prompt:
Build the one business website actually needed — not a site builder. A static site (home, services, about, contact) with copy in plain content files, so text edits never touch layout code. One mobile-first stylesheet using shared variables for brand colors and type, no framework or page-builder abstraction. A contact form that posts to a small server endpoint, emails you the message, and logs it as a fallback, with a honeypot field against spam. Generate SEO fundamentals automatically at build time: a sitemap, robots.txt, per-page meta tags, and a structured-data block with the business's name, hours, and address. If appointment booking matters, link out to a dedicated scheduling tool rather than building a booking engine here.

Do not build drag-and-drop editing, an app marketplace, or e-commerce — if the business genuinely needs a real store, that's a job for dedicated commerce software, not an extension of this site.

faq.q: Can I export my existing Wix site?
faq.a: Not really — Wix doesn't offer a structured content export. Copying the text and images over by hand into the new content files is realistic for a typical small-business site.

faq.q: Will it work on my phone?
faq.a: The published site is fully responsive. Editing content means editing files, which is a desktop task, not a phone one — that's the trade against Wix's own editor.

faq.q: What does it cost to run?
faq.a: Hosting and a domain, typically a few dollars a month, plus email delivery for the contact form — no per-app marketplace fees.

faq.q: What's the one thing that doesn't survive the rebuild?
faq.a: The app marketplace. Wix lets a non-technical owner add booking, chat, or loyalty features with a few clicks; here, each of those is a separate piece of software to integrate and maintain.
